title: Split a large file into parts and join it back with a checksum check
summary: Cuts a big file into numbered pieces, for example to fit a size limit, and joins the pieces back into one file. A SHA-256 checksum of the original, saved before splitting, proves that the joined file is identical.

aliases.text: split large file into parts and join back
split file linux and join again checksum
cut big file into pieces linux
split iso into chunks verify checksum
разрезать большой файл на части и склеить обратно
проверить контрольную сумму после склейки файла
разделить большой файл на части для флешки

steps.explain: Save the checksum of the original file. The line written to the .sha256 file is the proof you check the joined file against.
steps.expect: No output. The .sha256 file holds one line: a 64-character hex string and the file name.

steps.explain: Cut the file into pieces of 100 MB each. -d gives numbered suffixes and -a 3 uses three digits, so the pieces are part-000, part-001 and so on.
steps.expect: No output. New files named <FILE>.part-000, .part-001 and so on appear next to the original.

steps.explain: Join the pieces back into a new file. The glob lists the pieces in order because the numbers have the same width. The original is not touched.
steps.expect: No output. The joined file has the same size as the original.

steps.explain: Compare the checksum of the joined file with the saved one. MISMATCH means do not delete the parts or the original.

warnings: The pieces and the joined file take as much disk space as the original, so check free space first.
Quote file names with spaces, as the commands here do.
